svg.aria-label: How to write ુ ી: 2 parts, ુ, ી, one after another
svg.title: Writing ુ ી
svg.desc: 2 parts written one after another: ુ, ી (gujarati). The parts are in the order the hand writes them, which in Gujarati is the order they are typed: each sign comes after its consonant, even the i sign, which sits to the left of it. Each sign is drawn on its own, without the consonant it attaches to. Each part has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that part, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished part, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansGujarati-Static.ttf. Each part is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the parts are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: ુ: Tejas Gajjar, KanoAI, Gujarati barakhadi centre-line stroke templates (interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi), commit 9d3e294, 1_k/4_ku.svg, group g1 (stroke g1s0): the u sign drawn after the consonant (GitHub, 2026) <https://github.com/gajjartejas/KanoAI/tree/9d3e2949a3f265448e430e15329093ea3aa516b8/interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi>; ી: Tejas Gajjar, KanoAI, Gujarati barakhadi centre-line stroke templates (interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi), commit 9d3e294, 1_k/3_kee.svg, group g1 (stroke g1s0): the ii sign drawn after the consonant (GitHub, 2026) <https://github.com/gajjartejas/KanoAI/tree/9d3e2949a3f265448e430e15329093ea3aa516b8/interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi>. Source notes on variation: ુ: In the template for કુ, and in all 32 consonant rows whose consonant keeps its bare outline, ુ is one pen-down run that starts directly below the consonant, at the top of the sign, swings right and down round the bowl, and ends at its upper left. HP Labs India's Lipi Toolkit Devanagari recognizer (native writers' pen traces of the matching Devanagari sign, written alone) agrees: 79 of its 83 stored prototypes of the u sign (95%) are one stroke, and 82% of those turn clockwise. KanoAI's templates are hand-made centre lines, one path per pen-down run, which the app animates in the author's handwriting order and direction; one template per sign is placed beside every consonant, so the row counts show consistency, not separate writers. KanoAI's LICENSE file says MIT while its README says GNU GPL, so the licence is ambiguous: only facts are cited here (order, start, direction and pen lifts), and no template path data was copied. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Gujarati outline of the sign on its own. Handwriting varies by writer. ી: In the template for કી, and in all 34 consonant rows, ી is one pen-down run that starts at the left tip of the top hook, arches up and over to the right, comes down the right stem and ends in a foot to the right. HP Labs India's Lipi Toolkit Devanagari recognizer (native writers' pen traces of the matching Devanagari sign, written alone) agrees: its one-stroke prototypes of the ii sign (32 of 91, 35%) also start on the left and end at the lower right, though its most common form (51 of 91) is two strokes. KanoAI's templates are hand-made centre lines, one path per pen-down run, which the app animates in the author's handwriting order and direction; one template per sign is placed beside every consonant, so the row counts show consistency, not separate writers. KanoAI's LICENSE file says MIT while its README says GNU GPL, so the licence is ambiguous: only facts are cited here (order, start, direction and pen lifts), and no template path data was copied. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Gujarati outline of the sign on its own. Handwriting varies by writer.

svg.text: Part 1: stroke order after Tejas Gajjar, KanoAI, Gujarati barakhadi centre-line stroke templates (interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi), commit 9d3e294, 1_k/4_ku.svg, group g1 (stroke g1s0):
the u sign drawn after the consonant (GitHub, 2026)
Part 2: stroke order after Tejas Gajjar, KanoAI, Gujarati barakhadi centre-line stroke templates (interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi), commit 9d3e294, 1_k/3_kee.svg, group g1 (stroke g1s0):
the ii sign drawn after the consonant (GitHub, 2026)
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
